significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish both a causal decomposition—"shared mid-layer storage locus" with "format-specific access pathways" whose ablation selectively impairs one query format—and a form-(iii) predictive coupling in which facts with less circuit overlap have lower behavioral consistency. This would constrain expectations across cloze, question, multiple-choice, and translation queries: circuit divergence would predict retrieval inconsistency and distinguish access failure from absent storage, addressing the prompt-dependent factual recall documented by Jiang et al. (2020) and Elazar et al. (2021) rather than merely locating another factual representation. The phenomenon and mechanism are both definite; a negative result showing shared circuits or no overlap-consistency relationship would rule out this specific query-gated routing account, although it would not identify the alternative mechanism. In the topic-substitution check, the broad topic alone would not earn this score: the claim-specific shared-storage/different-access decomposition and measurable overlap-consistency law are what place it above the median hypothesis.

reach.justification: The transferable handles are the named "circuit-overlap (Jaccard)" score and "format-specific head" ablation targets, with the former serving as a potential predictor of which facts will be inconsistent across alternative query formats. That predictor can provide limited ex-ante lead time after circuits have been extracted but before relying on an untried phrasing; the component ablations themselves are primarily post-hoc mechanistic diagnostics. Re-extraction on a new model would not preserve particular heads, but the asserted relation—lower overlap predicts lower consistency—would still predict what should be found after recalibration across the stated class of factual-query formats, including cross-lingual prompts. Downstream uptake is mainly by factual-recall researchers and model auditors rather than general deployers, and the topic-substitution check does not preserve this score because the specific overlap metric and cross-format predictive relation, not knowledge retrieval generally, supply the reach.
